blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: compiler — Translates source to target code before execution.
interpreter — Executes by translating/evaluating at runtime.
assembler — Turns assembly into machine/object code.
object code — Compiled code awaiting linking or execution.

blocks.title: Compiler
blocks.text: Translates a complete source unit to target code before execution, often enabling optimisation.

blocks.title: Interpreter
blocks.text: Executes by translating/evaluating during running; behaviour varies by implementation.

blocks.title: Assembler
blocks.text: Converts symbolic assembly mnemonics into machine instructions.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: A compiler translates source to target machine/object code; linked executable can run without the source being present. Compilation can report syntax errors and apply optimisation before execution. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.

blocks.title: Shared worked answer
blocks.text: An assembler converts the mnemonic plus operand into its encoded machine instruction. In standard LMC, LDA 20 encodes as 520. This is not an interpreter translating a high-level language.
